reports.title: Definium Therapeutics Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Recent Highlights

desk.headline: Net loss narrows to $51.0m on warrant gain; $1.05bn cash funds plan into 2030, DT120 filing on track for H1 2027
results: Definium is a clinical-stage drug developer with no product revenue; its lead drug DT120 is a tablet form of LSD for anxiety and depression.
Two more Phase 3 studies in generalised anxiety (Voyage and Panorama) met their main and all key secondary goals, and DT120 won FDA Breakthrough status in depression.
Operating costs rose 58% to $72.3m as the company hired staff and prepared for a possible launch; R&D was $46.1m and G&A $26.1m.
The net loss narrowed to $51.0m (-$0.37 a share basic, -$0.46 diluted) from $67.3m, helped by a $12.4m gain on warrant revaluation and $10.1m of interest income.
Cash and investments rose to $1.05bn from $411.6m at end-2025 after share issuance; early results for autism candidate DT402 in five adults were described as positive.

guidance.summary: No revenue or earnings guidance, as usual for a clinical-stage company. Definium says its cash should fund operations into 2030 and it still plans to file DT120 for approval in the first half of 2027.

points: Management repeated that the DT120 approval filing is on track for H1 2027 but would not discuss the pre-filing FDA meeting until minutes are in hand.
Launch work is under way on market access, distribution and treatment sites; payers pointed to a price range of about $30,000-75,000 per treatment course.
The Ascend depression study is enrolling about 165 patients with results due in 2027; a PTSD Phase 3 and a multi-dose DT402 autism study are also planned for 2027.
Spending eased from Q2, though investment in commercial infrastructure will continue; a first Commercial Day is planned for H1 2027.
The CFO highlighted the balance sheet, saying few companies at this stage are as well funded.
